newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA FUEL OIL - MARKET STEADY AS BUYERS EMERGE.
newsitem.headline: ASIA FUEL OIL - MARKET STEADY AS BUYERS EMERGE.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market were steady on Friday as a Middle East trader emerged to support the market in the face of selling pressure from two majors, traders said.
"The market corrected itself yesterday and there was some recovery today because of the buying from the trader," one trader said.
Traders said the market was fundamentally tight due to lower crude runs and processing of less heavy crudes in favour of light crudes due to better prices of light and middle distillates.
Supplies from the Middle East were slightly below usual due to better demand there.

In the Singapore spot market, a European major sold to the Middle East trader 20,000 tonnes for August 23-27 lifting at $102.50 per tonne, 50 cents more than Thursday's traded level between the same two players.
Traders said there was buyer for 180-cst at $102 and for 380-cst at 99.00 per tonne, free-on-board basis.
Another cargo was offered for August 26-30 lifting at $103.00 per tonne.
The steady cargo trading was also reflected in the swaps market where prices edged up from the morning lows as the market recovered from the overnight crude losses.
August swaps traded from a day's low of $102.35 to $103.00.
Traders said firmer prices were also partly influenced by expectations of better bunker demand on news of the closure of South Korean ports as typhoon Tina approached the country's coast.
South Korean bunker sellers said they expected the ports to remain shut for two days until early Sunday.
Typhoon Tina also forced some oil refineries on the southern end of the Korean peninsular, such as Yukong Ltd and LG-Caltex Oil Corp, to close their terminals. Refinery output was not affected.

On Thursday, Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought two 0.5-percent sulphur low pour and one 1.0-percent low pour cargo at around $128.00 and $124.00 per tonnne, respectively, on a cost-and-freight basis.
